why: The definitions are the text's: maxPow E is literally ⋀[ℝ]^(dim E) E, maxPowDual E is Module.Dual ℝ (maxPow E), maxPowDualMap is the transpose of maxPowMap (B's (1), (2), (6) hold by rfl), and A's finrank_maxPow, maxPowMap_wedge, maxPowMap_ne_zero_iff, maxPowMap_comp, dualVec_self give B's (1), (3), (4), (5), (7) by instantiation. B ⇒ A uses B for finrank_maxPow, dualVec_self, eq_dualVec_of_apply_eq_one (B's v*(v)=1 plus 'a functional on a line is fixed by one value', dual_ext_of_ne_zero), maxPowMap_ne_zero_iff, and maxPowMap_wedge / maxPowMap_comp for finite-dimensional spaces. A has content B does not state, re-proved outright: the five wedge lemmas (wedge_eq_det_smul, wedge_append_basis_left/right, wedge_append_add_left/right — proof lemmas for Lemma 6.5, not claims of pp. 203–204), the general-k form of maxPowMap_wedge, and the infinite-dimensional cases of maxPowMap_wedge and maxPowMap_comp (A has no FiniteDimensional hypothesis there; B, like the text, speaks of finite-dimensional spaces).
overlap: 24 shared project theorems: the infrastructure behind the outright re-proofs of the wedge lemmas (alternatingMap_eq_det_smul, alternatingMap_eq_of_sub_mem_span, appendLeftMap/appendRightMap and their _proof_ terms, append_update_left/right, image_append_range_castAdd/natAdd), dual_ext_of_ne_zero and exists_smul_eq_of_finrank_eq_one (for eq_dualVec_of_apply_eq_one), and _proof_ terms of wedge, dualVec, maxPowMap.
